note: Car Garage (teen numbers plus ones, no carry). English only. Teaching has no question, so nothing to self-answer; the 1s pauses are beats before the next action. Type A (drag) = a*_a + a*_b + shared how_many: count the cars, drag the new ones into the ones garage, then answer the total. a4_b reuses a1_b because both say the same sentence. Type B (pick) = b*_q, three garage cards mixing parked and incoming cars. Type C (touch) = c*_q, one sentence pair per file. Runtime shuffles the ten questions and every option set.

lines.text: Look at the garage! Here is one full row of ten cars.
And two more cars. That's twelve cars.
Now, three new cars are coming.
We put the new cars in the ones garage.
Two cars plus three cars equals five cars.
So, twelve plus three equals fifteen! One ten and five ones.
When we add, the ten garage stays the same.
We only add the ones garage.
There are thirteen cars.
Drag two more cars into the ones garage.
There are fourteen cars.
Drag three more cars into the ones garage.
There are eleven cars.
Drag five more cars into the ones garage.
There are sixteen cars.
How many cars in total?
Find twelve plus three.
Find thirteen plus four.
Find eleven plus five.
Fourteen plus three. Touch the correct number.
Twelve plus six. Touch the correct number.
Fifteen plus four. Touch the correct number.
